description: Somos un equipo de desarrolladores apasionados por la tecnología, la innovación y la exploración espacial. Nos motiva convertir ideas ambiciosas en soluciones reales mediante programación, IA, análisis de datos y trabajo colaborativo. Nuestro objetivo es ganar y divertirnos construyendo un proyecto creativo con impacto.
summary: Lunar Mission Navigator is a web simulator that helps choose where and when to land at the Moon’s south pole. Using real NASA data (JPL Horizons ephemerides and LOLA terrain), it calculates in seconds whether the lander will have sunlight for its solar panels, enough battery, and a direct line of sight to Earth without a relay satellite. It compares up to four scenarios, shows how the verdict changes if launch slips, and uses a 37-cell honeycomb to find nearby sites with better horizons. Its key insight is that small changes in coordinates have a large impact: at Shackleton, sunlight is roughly 25% of the year, while a point a few kilometers away on the rim reaches roughly 70%. The app makes this visible for technical users and students alike, and it reduces mission planning from days to seconds.
details:
What it does: For a landing site and date, the simulator models solar power, battery state, surface temperature, and the communication link to Earth. It then gives a green, yellow, or red verdict based on the real mission duration.
How it works: Hourly ephemerides from JPL Horizons, LOLA terrain for a 360-degree horizon, and a lunar globe with LROC textures. The calculations run in the browser.
Tools: Next.js, React, TypeScript, React Three Fiber, Zustand, Tailwind CSS, and CopilotKit for the assistant.
Creativity: The honeycomb shows how suitability changes cell by cell, and a narrated demo explains the problem in one minute.
Expected impact: Faster lunar landing site planning with more data, with a simple mode for students and a technical mode for specialists.
